title: Water Drifts to the Saltier Side

scenes.visual: Title card 'Water Drifts to the Saltier Side' over a cucumber slice with salt sprinkled on top. COLOUR MAP (both films): membrane = WHITE DASHED vertical line on a dark navy background; dye = small PURPLE dots; water = small BLUE dots; salt = small GREY squares; oxygen = small GREEN dots; carbon dioxide = small RED dots. Crossing tallies = WHITE arrows with counters above the membrane, '→ N' for left to right and '← N' for right to left. Every tank and cell is a cartoon labelled 'schematic'. Numbers appear only as on-screen text. Same colours and tally arrows as the first film.

scenes.tts: Remember the salted cucumber? Drops of water bead up on top, and nobody squeezed it. So where did that water come from, and what made it leave?
scenes.visual: Cartoon cucumber slice on a plate. Salt crystals fall on it. A clock face sweeps to the on-screen text '15 min' and small water beads swell up on the slice. Question card: 'where did the water come from?'
scenes.narration: Remember the salted cucumber? Drops of water bead up on top, and nobody squeezed it. So where did that water come from, and what made it leave?

scenes.tts: The first film showed random hops making a one-way drift, from crowded to less crowded. This time, the crowded particle is salt, and the membrane holds it back.
scenes.visual: Brief replay of the first film's tank with purple dots and tally arrows '→ 3, ← 1'. Then the purple dots fade and grey salt squares take their place, bouncing off the white dashed membrane.
scenes.narration: The first film showed random hops making a one-way drift, from crowded to less crowded. This time, the crowded particle is salt, and the membrane holds it back.

scenes.tts: Here is the same tank and membrane. Blue water dots fill both sides. Grey salt squares sit only on the right. In this model, the membrane holds back all the salt. Real ones let a little through, much more slowly.
scenes.visual: Navy tank labelled 'schematic', white dashed membrane in the middle. Blue water dots jiggle on both sides; grey squares only on the right, each bouncing off the membrane when it reaches it. Small corner label: 'model: all salt held back'.
scenes.narration: Here is the same tank and membrane. Blue water dots fill both sides. Grey salt squares sit only on the right. In this model, the membrane holds back all the salt. Real ones let a little through, much more slowly.

scenes.tts: Now take a spoonful from each side. On the left, every space holds water. On the right, some spaces hold salt instead. So the right side has less water.
scenes.visual: A white spoon outline scoops a 10-space grid from each side. Left grid: 10 blue dots, on-screen 'water: 10 of 10'. Right grid: 7 blue dots and 3 grey squares, on-screen 'water: 7 of 10'. Small label on both grids: 'cartoon spaces, not real ones'.
scenes.narration: Now take a spoonful from each side. On the left, every space holds water. On the right, some spaces hold salt instead. So the right side has less water.

scenes.tts: This grid is only a cartoon. We drew far more salt than is real, so you can see it. Real salt water is still almost all water. The difference is small, but it is there.
scenes.visual: A banner across the right grid: 'salt exaggerated so you can see it'. The grey squares shrink to tiny specks among many blue dots, then grow back to drawing size.
scenes.narration: This grid is only a cartoon. We drew far more salt than is real, so you can see it. Real salt water is still almost all water. The difference is small, but it is there.

scenes.tts: Water dots hop at random, both ways. So which way will more water dots cross? Toward the side with more water, or toward the side with less? Pause and decide.
scenes.visual: The tank freezes. Pause card: 'Which way will MORE water dots cross?' with buttons '→ toward the salt side' and '← toward the plain side'. Ring timer appears.
scenes.narration: Water dots hop at random, both ways. So which way will more water dots cross? Toward the side with more water, or toward the side with less? Pause and decide.

scenes.visual: Pause card holds; ring timer runs down.

scenes.tts: On average, more water crosses from the left, where there is more water. Nothing pulls it. There is simply more water on the left to make the hop.
scenes.visual: Motion resumes. Blue tally arrows fire: '→ 5', '← 3'. The water level on the right slowly rises above the left. Salt squares keep bouncing off the membrane. Small text: 'nothing pulls the water'.
scenes.narration: On average, more water crosses from the left, where there is more water. Nothing pulls it. There is simply more water on the left to make the hop.

scenes.tts: This drift of water across a selectively permeable membrane is called osmosis. Water moves from more water to less water. That is the side with more dissolved particles.
scenes.visual: The word 'osmosis' writes on screen: 'diffusion of water across a selectively permeable membrane'. Below it, a two-part arrow: 'more water → less water' on top and 'fewer dissolved particles → more dissolved particles' beneath, both pointing right.
scenes.narration: This drift of water across a selectively permeable membrane is called osmosis. Water moves from more water to less water. That is the side with more dissolved particles.

scenes.tts: Back to the cucumber. Zoom into one cell. Salt sits outside, and the membrane holds most of it back. The salty liquid has more dissolved particles than the cell does. So there is less water outside.
scenes.visual: Zoom from the cucumber slice into one boxy cartoon plant cell, labelled 'schematic': green wall, white dashed membrane, a large pale-blue vacuole. Many grey squares crowd outside; a few grey squares sit inside the cell; blue dots inside and out.
scenes.narration: Back to the cucumber. Zoom into one cell. Salt sits outside, and the membrane holds most of it back. The salty liquid has more dissolved particles than the cell does. So there is less water outside.

scenes.tts: Water drifts out of the cell, toward the salty side. The vacuole shrinks, and water beads up on the slice.
scenes.visual: Blue tally arrows show more water leaving than entering ('→ out' larger than '← in'). The vacuole shrinks; the membrane pulls slightly inward. Zoom out: beads of water on the slice.
scenes.narration: Water drifts out of the cell, toward the salty side. The vacuole shrinks, and water beads up on the slice.

scenes.tts: A limp lettuce leaf sits in plain water. Its cells hold more dissolved particles than the water around them, so there is less water inside.
scenes.visual: Cut to a limp lettuce leaf drooping in a bowl of water. Zoom into one leaf cell, labelled 'schematic': small vacuole, a few grey squares inside, almost none outside.
scenes.narration: A limp lettuce leaf sits in plain water. Its cells hold more dissolved particles than the water around them, so there is less water inside.

scenes.tts: So water drifts in. The vacuole fills, and the cell presses out against its stiff wall. The wall presses back. The cells firm up, and the leaf turns crisp.
scenes.visual: Blue tally arrows now show more water entering. The vacuole swells and the cell presses against the green wall; small outward arrows labelled 'presses on wall' and small inward arrows from the wall labelled 'wall presses back'. Zoom out: the lettuce leaf straightens and turns crisp.
scenes.narration: So water drifts in. The vacuole fills, and the cell presses out against its stiff wall. The wall presses back. The cells firm up, and the leaf turns crisp.

scenes.tts: In both cases, the cell spent no energy moving the water. Osmosis is passive transport. It is the same random drift from the first film. In our model, only water crosses.
scenes.visual: Side by side: the shrunken cucumber cell and the full lettuce cell, each with a full battery icon labelled 'no energy spent'. Above them, the first film's tank with purple dots flashes briefly, then turns into the water tank.
scenes.narration: In both cases, the cell spent no energy moving the water. Osmosis is passive transport. It is the same random drift from the first film. In our model, only water crosses.

scenes.tts: So follow the water. When the membrane holds the salt back, water drifts toward more dissolved particles. A push back, like a stiff wall, can slow or stop that drift.
scenes.visual: The two-part arrow from the osmosis scene returns over the tank: 'more water → less water' and 'fewer dissolved particles → more dissolved particles'. A small green wall segment appears at the right edge with an inward arrow labelled 'push back can stop the drift'.
scenes.narration: So follow the water. When the membrane holds the salt back, water drifts toward more dissolved particles. A push back, like a stiff wall, can slow or stop that drift.

scenes.visual: Hex end card. Line: 'Water drifts toward more dissolved particles, unless something pushes back.'
